title: Scenario laddering: headcount & pricing heuristics (Q3 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc outlines a laddered scenario framework to couple headcount plans with near-term pricing sensitivity gates. Goal is to produce a compact operational playbook (for FY27 Q3–Q4 execution) that: 1) preserves runway when model/compression shocks hit, 2) allows targeted hires to continue for high-leverage engineering/product work, and 3) sequences price changes with minimum churn risk.

Context / why now:
- Market pricing pressure for hosted inference has accelerated (spot/hosted price compression in H1–H2 2026).
- Multiple teams (product, infra, SRE) flagged capacity constraints that require hiring but budget is constrained.
- We need an executable mapping from price-change triggers -> hiring actions -> runway impact to brief execs and sales.

High-level approach (laddering):
Create 4 operational tiers (Green / Yellow / Orange / Red) defined by a combination of: realized ARR movement, per-token gross margin delta, and 12-week runway buffer. For each tier we define: price-action(s), hiring actions (freeze/slow/hire), and short-term cost levers (burst reserve, contractor swap, quantization push).

Definitions / inputs (assumptions for sensitivity):
- Base burn (CB): $6.3M/month (includes committed infra + S&M + R&D amortized).
- Base headcount FTE: 150 (as of 2026-10).
- Avg fully-loaded cost per FTE (FLC): $17.5k/month (salary + benefits + ops).
- Token-driven margin sensitivity (per 10% price compression on hosted units): -$0.22M/month to gross margin (empirical from H1 2026).
- Elasticity range for customer churn vs price increase: 0.05–0.25 (conservative to aggressive).
- Target runway floor (operational): 18 months at Green; tactical buffer at Yellow: 12 months; critical buffer (Red): 6 months.

Quick scenario table (snapshot):
Scenario, Price change (hosted avg), Gross margin delta/mo, Headcount action, Monthly burn delta
Green, +0% to +3%, 0 to +0.1M, Continue hires, +0.0M
Yellow, -5% price compression, -0.22M, Pause non-core hiring, -0.52M (partial contractor swap + reduced hiring)
Orange, -12% price compression OR ARR down 8% q/q, -0.55M, Targeted 10% FTE slow (15 hires paused), -1.65M (reduces burn via hiring pause + hire->contract swap)
Red, -20% price compression OR ARR down 20% q/q, -1.1M, Hiring freeze + 8% layoffs (12–14 roles), -2.95M (compounded)

Notes on numbers: the burn deltas in the rightmost column include: immediate savings from hiring pause (phased over 2–6 months), contractor conversion costs, and one-time severance bucket amortized. We assume ~40% of R&D hiring is deferrable without immediate product revenue impact for up to 12 weeks.

Operational gates (concrete triggers):
1) Margin Gate: If rolling 6-week gross margin decline > 6% vs baseline -> move to Yellow.
2) ARR Gate: If trailing 8-week ARR net-retention < 92% -> move to Orange.
3) Price Shock Gate: If average realized market price compression (public indicators + telemetry) > 10% AND sales pipeline conversion drops > 5ppt -> move to Orange.
4) Runway Gate: If forecasted runway falling below 9 months -> escalate to exec and prepare Red actions.

Action matrix (what to do at each tier):
Green: continue planned hiring (prioritize SRE & infra), maintain burst capacity, increase Optimize experiments (aggressively run quantization & batching experiments).
Yellow: pause all non-customer-facing hires and freeze hiring in non-core teams (internal infra non-critical roles). Pull forward Optimize quick wins (kv prefix cache rollout). Evaluate 6-8 week contractor replacements for non-critical work.
Orange: enforce targeted hiring pause across 10% of headcount plan, delay non-essential product launches, reallocate hiring budget to SRE/serving-runtime. Start 60-day attrition review and reorg options for overlapping roles. Re-price renewal offers for >=$250k customers with caution (A/B test).
Red: full hiring freeze, execute 6–10% workforce realignment (with severance fund drawn from contingency bucket). Activate price increases (tiered) for new customers first, implement aggressive cost-of-serve reductions (higher quantization levels, reduce burst pools), postpone non-critical capital commitments.

Pricing levers & sequencing guidance:
- Sequence A (low-risk): Adjust tiered overage pricing for very high QPS customers; add surcharge for non-committed burst capacity. Communicate as product feature (burst surcharge) not coercive price increase.
- Sequence B (medium-risk): Small list price increases (3–7%) for new signups + renegotiation window for existing customers with 60–90 day notice; pair with improved SLI/SLA packaging to reduce churn risk.
- Sequence C (high-risk): Broad per-token pricing increase; only if runway triggers force it (Red). Use grandfathering rules for legacy customers for 6 months to blunt churn.

Sensitivity experiments to run (short-term):
1) Elasticity matrix: run customer-level simulation using elasticity range [0.05, 0.25] across top 200 customers to quantify churn risk for each price band (3%, 7%, 12%).
2) Headcount ramp curve: model hiring pause vs. organic attrition interplay across 6–24 weeks; estimate time-to-market impact for 3 product initiatives.
3) Quantization savings tuning: simulate cost-of-serve reduction for mixed quantization (int8 + 4-bit-quant for <SLO requests) and estimate quality/regression risk per model family.

Example quick math (back-of-envelope):
- Pause 15 hires planned in next 3 months -> saves ~15 * $17.5k = $262.5k/mo after hiring window (phased). Over 6 months ~ $1.6M saved (gross).
- If hosted token price compresses 12% -> M/delta = -$0.55M/mo. Hiring pause above covers ~48% of that shortfall after 2 months.

Communication & cadence:
- Weekly signal deck (Finance -> Exec) with: 6-week gross margin, rolling ARR, top-20 customer callouts, projected runway at current burn, recommended tier.
- If tier moves Yellow/Orange: 24-hour cross-functional review with Product/OPS/Sales. Define top-3 mitigation actions and owner.
- If moving to Red: 72-hour Exec decision window, immediate hiring freeze, prepare layoff/offer pause comms in <5 business days.

Open questions / TODOs (for next 10 days):
- [Econ] Re-run elasticity exercise on cohort-level (North America SaaS vs enterprise). Owner: Marcus (due: 2026-11-12).
- [People] Confirm severance fund availability for 8–10% realignment. Owner: Priya (due: 2026-11-09).
- [Product] Prioritize 3 Optimize experiments that can be shipped in 4 weeks. Owner: Ben (due: 2026-11-18).
- [Sales] Define grandfathering and notice templates for price changes; collect top-50 renewals calendar. Owner: Sales Ops (due: 2026-11-20).

Appendix: minimal scenario model snippet (paste into sheet):
Columns: month, base_burn, planned_hires, hires_paused, effective_burn, runway_months
2026-11, 6.3M, 6, 0, 6.3M, 17.4
2026-12, 6.45M, 8, 2, 6.1M, 18.0
2027-01, 6.2M, 10, 8, 5.7M, 19.5
(note: simplistic; use linked sheet for detailed phasing)

Bottom line (summary):
We need an operational ladder (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red) that ties objective telemetry -> pricing actions -> headcount changes. The ladder must be small, executable, and owner-driven. Next step: run the elasticity matrix and finalize triggers (we have the framework above).

Comments welcome — leave inline notes. This doc is intentionally compact; will expand with model outputs once Marcus' simulation is ready.

-- Eleanor
